newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A proposed law has recommended setting up of separate loan courts and enactment of tougher laws providing for civil prison for bank loan defaulters.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Friday said her government would protect the interest of the workers during reforms.
The Burmese authorities on Friday suspended the repatriation of Rohingya refugees for the second time in a month.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Friday said the government would give priority to any plan of the labourers to buy the closed mills and factories to run those through cooperatives.
Former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad has brought back former Prime Minister Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury to the position of the first vice-chairman of his Jatiya Party.
President Alberto Fujimoro of Peru will visit Bangladesh on May 24-25.
Bangladesh has been reelected as a member of the United Nations Commission on Human Rights (UNCHR).
The World Bank released $168.5 million in project loan to Bangladesh during the first seven months of the current fiscal year (July'96-Jan'97).
